items.title: DroppedNeedle Is a Self-Hosted Music Request and Discovery App
items.summary: Running your own music server is great, but finding new albums, downloading them, and getting everything properly organized can still involve quite a bit of manual work. Even with something like Jellyfin or Navidrome handling playback, managing the music that actually ends up in your library is another story. DroppedNeedle aims to simplify that process by bringing music requests, downloads, discovery, and library management into one self-hosted interface. Music Requests and Library Management DroppedNeedle is an open-source music management application that uses MusicBrainz to search for artists, albums, and individual tracks.

items.title: What Can't Be Self-Hosted? Reddit Has Some Interesting Answers
items.summary: I've been self-hosting long enough to know how it goes. You get one service running on your own hardware, then start looking at the next thing you can move off somebody else's servers. Eventually, you start wondering how far you can take it. Are there things you simply can't self-host? That question came up in a recent r/selfhosted discussion started by Reddit user u/Scandinavianplunger. The answers were interesting, particularly because some of the suggestions had people disagreeing with each other.

items.title: Chronicles: Medieval devs Raw Power are bankrupt, but their sandbox RPG lives on at a new studio co-founded by Satisfactory devs Coffee Stain

The game will now be made by a new developer, owned 25% by a few former Raw Power devs and 75% by Coffee Stain. Coffee Stain will fund the game's on-going development.

items.title: Recall petition filed against El Mirage vice mayor as residents clash over her leadership
items.summary: A group of El Mirage residents is moving forward with an effort to recall Vice Mayor Jacquelyn Parsons, accusing her of failing to deliver on campaign promises. But supporters of Parsons are pushing back, calling the effort a political power play. Recall organizers submitted their petition Tuesday after collecting more than 720 signatures, exceeding the 647 required to potentially trigger a recall election. For residents leading the effort, the petition is about holding elected officials accountable.

items.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
items.summary: External sandboxes for coding agents I've been exploring new ways to sandbox code that is executed by agents, with a focus on making it safer to try out local models without worrying that a mistake or prompt injection attack might cause them to take damaging actions on a machine. I worked on this project with Prime Radiant, the AI research lab behind Superpowers and other projects. My post on the Prime Radiant blog introduces the external sandbox pattern, where code executed by the agent runs inside a dedicated sandbox while the agent itself lives outside of that sandbox.

You may think of it as a successor to the popular STM32-based Flipper Zero hardware and wireless hacking tool, but the company stresses that the Flipper One is NOT a replacement for the Flipper Zero.

items.title: Multikernel Linux Comes To ARM64, mklinux 7.0-mk5 Released
items.summary: The out-of-tree Multikernel Linux patches for allowing multiple independent kernel instances to run on the same physical machine is out with a new version. The multi-kernel architecture is interesting for fail-safe kernel purposes, running an RT kernel on certain CPU cores and other non-traditional compute purposes. Multikernel was also demonstrated recently with Kmorph for reboot-less Linux kernel crash recovery. Out now is mklinux 7.0-mk5 as the latest iteration of these Multikernel patches based atop the upstream Linux 7.0 kernel.

items.title: FAA’s Flight Shutdown Fuels A $30 Billion Funding Push—Most Of The Money Isn’t Even For Air Traffic Control
items.summary: After the FAA communications breakdown brought departures across the country to a halt on Friday, the travel industry has its answer: give air traffic control another $30 billion. Most of the money in the bill they're pushing wouldn't even go to air traffic control.

items.title: Grok Bot took unapproved actions, ignored orders to stop, and then denied it
items.summary: Researchers recently discovered unexpected behavior from Grok Bot, the AI agent platform from Elon Musk’s SpaceXSI. Over five days, Grok bots installed on two separate employee laptops made 31 requests to access data stored in employee calendar, email, Slack, and GitHub accounts. The bots performed the actions even though the employees had never ordered them and continued doing them even after employees instructed them to stop. The bots also denied having taken the actions at all. The behavior was reported Tuesday by NewCore, the maker of a managed gateway product that acts as an intermediary between AI agents and the tools and accounts they are assigned to work with.

items.title: NextCloud Has Launched an Office Suite for Desktop Users
items.summary: Nextcloud's office editors already work in the browser, and as of a few days ago, there is an open source desktop app that should appeal to a wider userbase that prefers doing their document work locally. The app is based on the DesktopEditors code of Euro-Office, which, as you might remember, is a coalition of European companies that includes Nextcloud, IONOS, Proton, Open-Xchange, and Tuta. Its primary aim is to offer open and sovereign document editing, with its first production-ready version coming out back in June.

items.title: Controllers question official explanation for US air traffic control outage
items.summary: Air traffic controllers and a former senior accident investigator are questioning the US government’s explanation for the November 13, 2026, communications failure that halted departures across the country for more than four hours. Four days after the disruption, the controllers’ union says the FAA has yet to brief its workforce on the specific cause of the outage, and controllers say they want answers. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said it has traced the disruption to excessive data flooding its telecommunications network after contractor L3Harris installed a router at a remote radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas.

items.title: Soverin Suite Joins a Growing Wave of European Companies Selling "Sovereignty as a Service"
items.summary: Switching away from Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace is easy to talk about. Actually doing it is a different story altogether. Somebody has to set up the servers, keep them patched, migrate the mails, and then teach people to use the new software and that's probably the hardest part. That is the gap a new breed of European companies is trying to fill. They don't write the software from scratch. They take open source tools like Nextcloud and Euro-Office, run them on European hardware, and sell it as a ready-to-use service with support in their package.

items.title: Buckeye officer injured after suspected drunken driver rams patrol vehicles
items.summary: BUCKEYE, AZ A Buckeye police officer is recovering after a suspected drunken driver slammed into the officers patrol vehicle Monday night. At around 7:45 p.m., officers responded to a report of a reckless driver in a pickup truck exiting Interstate 10 at Watson Road. Officers spotted the truck and followed it into a neighborhood, where it was seen swerving on the street. When an officer attempted to pull the driver over, the driver sped away but lost control of the truck and slammed into a wall near 230th Drive and Morning Glory Street.

items.title: GIMP Adds Automated UI Testing for Linux X11 and Wayland
items.summary: GIMP has introduced a new automated GUI testing system to catch bugs and regressions before they reach users. The infrastructure allows developers to test actual interactions with the application, including menus, dialogs, buttons, and common image-editing operations. Until now, GIMP relied on unit tests and other methods that interact with its internal code. According to the devs, while useful for checking individual components, these approaches cannot always detect problems that appear when users interact with the graphical interface.

items.title: NASA Launches Nuclear Power Systems Student Contest
items.summary: NASA’s Power to Explore Student Challenge kicked off Tuesday, Nov. 17. The science, engineering, technology, and mathematics (STEM) challenge invites kindergarten through 12th grade students in the United States to learn about space nuclear power systems and illustrate how these nuclear “batteries” could help power their lunar exploration vision. Students are also invited to write a short essay about a “superpower” of their own. Submissions are due March 1, 2027. Every mission requires a power source.

items.title: NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records
items.summary: 2 min read NASA Space Apps Challenge Breaks Global Hackathon Records On Nov. 14 and 15, NASA held the annual Space Apps Challenge with a record-breaking 181,835 registered participants taking part in 593 events around the world. The annual hackathon invites participants to use NASA’s open data to address one of 14 challenges focused on space exploration or Earth science. This year, the hackathon drew 59% more registrants and was the 5th year in a row with increased participation. Since 2012, NASA Space Apps Challenge has hosted the two-day event, which has included more than 600,000 people from more than 190 countries.

items.title: New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra
items.summary: 4 Min Read New Album of Baby Star Sounds Shared by NASA’s Chandra A new album from NASA’s Chandra X-ray Observatory collects snapshots of baby stars across the galaxy and beyond and transforms that data into sound. Four new sonifications use data of stars that are actively forming, captured by Chandra and other NASA telescopes By studying places in the universe where stars are currently being born and young stars are present, astronomers can better understand the lifecycle of all stars, including our own Sun.

items.title: Senators Urge FAA to Pause Router Installations Following Ground Stop
items.summary: Thirteen Democratic senators on the Senate Commerce Committee are calling on the FAA to temporarily halt installation of new communications routers following Friday’s nationwide ground stop. In a letter reported by Reuters on Tuesday, the lawmakers, led by Sen. Maria Cantwell of Washington, urged the agency to address potential safety and reliability concerns before continuing its telecommunications modernization program. The request follows a nearly five-hour ground stop on Nov. 13 that resulted in more than 18,000 canceled flights.

items.title: NASA to Cover 35th SpaceX Resupply Mission Space Station Departure
items.summary: NASA and its international partners are set to receive scientific research samples and hardware as a SpaceX Dragon spacecraft departs the International Space Station no earlier than Wednesday, Nov. 18, for its return to Earth. Pending weather conditions, the Dragon spacecraft will undock from the Harmony module’s space-facing port at 11:05 a.m. EST, following a command sent by ground controllers at SpaceX’s facility in Hawthorne, California. NASA’s live coverage of undocking and departure begins at 10:45 a.m., streaming through a variety of platforms.

items.title: Chilly morning as approaching storm brings snow up north; Phoenix stays dry
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — It’s a chilly start to the day, with Valley temperatures in the 40s under mostly clear skies with light winds. Afternoon temperatures will climb to the low 70s, which is slightly cooler than average. As a trough of low pressure that brought rain to Arizona on Tuesday moves away today, look for sunshine and light winds. Another storm will move onshore in California today, and swing by to the north of Arizona on Thursday and Friday. While the Valley is expected to stay dry, this will reinforce the cooler air in place across the Southwest, keeping temperatures on the cool side through the weekend.

items.title: RBRD: RAM-Backed Linux Block Driver Written In Rust For Better Safety But Slower Performance
items.summary: Linux kernel patches were posted tonight for introducing RBRD, the RAM-backed block driver written in the Rust programming language. Linux has the BRD Driver currently that provides a RAM-backed block device driver written in C code for providing a virtual block device. RBRD is now a Rust-based version of this "true" block device implementation in RAM. Granted, with today's memory pricing and availability, RAM-based block device usage is likely limited but still useful for simulations and speedy testing.

items.title: Two Independent Projects Want to Bring MATE to Wayland, Each in its Own Way
items.summary: The big Linux desktop environments have largely made up their minds about Wayland. GNOME finished removing X11 from its login manager in March, and last month, KDE Plasma retired support for starting X11 sessions. Cinnamon is a step behind, but Linux Mint 27, due around Christmas, is set to ship a Wayland session that is no longer experimental. Though X11 stays the default. Smaller desktops are at different points on the same journey. LXQt dropped the experimental label from its Wayland session in v2.3.0, and Budgie in the Ubuntu Budgie 26.04 release went Wayland-only with labwc.

items.title: Arizona vaccination rates raise concerns as US loses measles elimination status
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — The United States has lost its measles elimination status, and health experts say low vaccination rates in Arizona have contributed to the disease’s resurgence. Arizona reported five measles cases in 2024 and 222 in 2025, the third-highest total in the country. The state currently ranks 13th nationally. Vaccination rates and exemptions The U.S. first eliminated measles in 2000. Dr. Rebecca Sunenshine, the medical director of the health observatory at Arizona State University, said the virus can now spread effectively from person to person.

items.title: FAA ground stop put focus on air traffic controller shortages at Phoenix Sky Harbor, nationwide
items.summary: WASHINGTON – The ground stop Friday that halted flights nationwide did not result from the chronic shortage of air traffic controllers. But managing the roughly 3,500 planes in the air did test an understaffed system that relies on controller overtime to meet operational demand. At Phoenix Sky Harbor, the Federal Aviation Administration has blamed a number of incidents in recent months on the staffing shortages, including a ground stop and flight delays within a week last month. Despite the shortages in Phoenix and around the country, the rare and potentially chaotic nationwide ground stop was executed smoothly.

But Voyager 1 launched on a faster trajectory than its twin and has just become the first spacecraft to ever reach one light-day away, which is equivalent to about 16 billion miles (about 26 billion kilometers), or the distance that one light particle travels in 24 hours. items.title: Rocket Lab’s Electron completes 100th mission, Neutron progresses toward debut mission
items.summary: Last weekend, Rocket Lab’s workhorse Electron rocket officially completed its 100th mission, becoming the fastest commercially developed rocket to reach the milestone. The company has also been achieving several hardware milestones for its upcoming partially reusable Neutron vehicle. Electron’s achievement caps a defining year for the company, which has steadily evolved from a dedicated small-satellite launcher into a vertically integrated aerospace prime contractor that is capable of building several components of spaceflight systems.

items.title: Black Holes and Their Mysterious Bright Structures Explained
items.summary: Black hole jets from the SMBH in Centaurus A, and from some other SMBH, are brighter on their edges than in their centers. It's called limb brightening, and it's unexpected, and astrophysicists want to know what causes it. They found their answer in detailed plasma physics simulations, and the results could also help efforts to develop fusion power.

items.title: Helping AI text detectors keep up with changing conditions
items.summary: A teacher who believes a student’s term paper may have been written by a large language model (LLM) can use a tool for detecting artificial intelligence-generated text to help confirm their suspicions. But the teacher may want to think twice before putting all their trust in the detector. Researchers from MIT and Cornell University showed that such detection tools, which are AI models themselves, can be fooled by AI-generated text disguised to appear as if it were written by a human. Detectors can also fail to identify AI text due to natural shifts in writing habits over time or the emergence of new LLMs.

items.title: 'It looked like every star in the sky was falling': Eyewitnesses remember the great Leonid meteor storm of 1966
items.summary: Overnight Nov. 17-18, 1966, the Leonid meteor storm thrilled stargazers during one extraordinary night when the stars themselves looked as though they were falling from the sky. At the peak of the shower, observers at Kitt Peak National Observatory in Arizona estimated an astonishing 40 meteors per second streaking across the sky. That's 2,400 shooting stars per minute, or a staggering 144,000 per hour. It was a spectacle that many regard as the greatest meteor display in recorded history. It's hard to imagine what it was like to experience such a spectacle.

items.title: Voyager 1 at one light-day: Historian revisits Golden Record's forgotten details
items.summary: In the one light-day that humanity's most distant object has now traveled from Earth, there has been enough time for details about its creation—and what it left behind—to be discovered again. Voyager 1, which left Earth in 1977 on an initial mission to fly by Jupiter and Saturn (as well as the latter's moon Titan), crossed into interstellar space in 2012. Like its twin (Voyager 2), Voyager 1 carries a "commemorative phonograph record," in part as a nod to the 100th anniversary of the recording medium and as a message from humanity to whoever (or whatever) encounters the spacecraft on its journey through outer space.

items.title: Arizona voters will decide the future of photo enforcement cameras in cities like Mesa
items.summary: Arizona voters will decide whether cities like Mesa can keep their speed and red-light cameras. On Nov. 3, 61% of Arizona voters approved Proposition 319. The measure bans cities and towns from adding new photo enforcement cameras. It also requires cities that already use the cameras to ask their own voters whether to keep them. A city spokesperson says Mesa runs intersection safety cameras at 17 locations and in nine school zones. At Highland Junior High School, Mesa police use a portable camera system to enforce the speed limit around campus.

items.title: Bottles 67.7 Improves Windows App Compatibility on Linux
items.summary: Bottles 67.7 has been released as a maintenance update for the Linux application that makes running Windows software and games using Wine easier. One important fix concerns dependency installation. Previously, Bottles could fail to identify the Windows version correctly when Wine produced diagnostic messages or wrote to stderr, which could prevent dependency installers from running. Version 67.7 corrects this, allowing the Windows version to be detected properly in these situations. The update also improves synchronization handling for Windows games.

items.title: ‘3 Body Problem’ Season 2 Teases Its Chaotic Alien Invasion
items.summary: Cast your mind backâway backâto early 2024, when Netflix released season one of its 3 Body Problem adaptation. At last, the show from Alexander Woo and Game of Thrones creators David Benioff and D.B. Weiss is making its return. It will touch down on the streamer January 14 for its six-episode second season (season one was eight episodes), and an absolutely blistering first teaser has just arrived. With three total seasons planned, season two will continue the narrative of Cixin Liu’s blockbuster Remembrance of Earth’s Past novel trilogy, with some creative license taken to help make the sprawling story fit into a TV series format.

items.title: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol
items.summary: GPT‑6.2 Astra and GPT‑6.2 Sol OpenAI: We’re introducing GPT‑6.2 Astra, our new frontier model for your hardest projects, and GPT‑6.2 Sol, our efficient, versatile model for everyday work. They're available in the API as gpt-6.2-astra and gpt-6.2-sol. I shipped LLM 0.38 with support for the new models. 6.2 Astra is 80% of the price of 6 Astra - $8/MTok input and $40/MTok output, the same price as Claude Fable 5.2 (which was also 80% of its predecessor). 6 Astra and Fable 5 were both $10/$50. The cached price is an even bigger discount - $0.40/million compared to $1/million for the older model.

items.title: Real-Life Superhero Documentary ‘Phoenix Jones’ Sets Netflix Streaming Debut
items.summary: One of the more talked-about documentaries out of this year's SXSW is headed to Netflix. Phoenix Jones: The Rise and Fall of a Real Life Superhero will make its streaming debut on Netflix in the United States on December 12th, 2026. Directed by Bayan Joonam in his feature debut, the documentary first premiered in the Documentary Feature Competition at the SXSW Film & TV Festival back in March before going on to play a hometown screening at the Seattle International Film Festival. At the time…

items.title: AMD Gets Its Firmware Ready For Upcoming RDNA 4m iGPUs On Linux
items.summary: AMD overnight merged the latest changes of the open-source graphics driver puzzle for the upcoming RDNA 4m "GFX17x" iGPUs on Linux. The firmware is ready for enabling the next-gen AMD iGPUs on Linux. Going back to February we have been seeing a lot of AMD open-source driver enablement work around the GFX117 series as a new target and bridge between the existing GFX11.5 "RDNA 3.5" refresh iGPUs and the GFX12 "RDNA 4" GPUs. Patches have referred to GFX117x as " RDNA 4m " with some ISA differences over RDNA 3.5 indicating its more than a simple rebranding or marketing push.

items.title: How AI is pushing satellites to evolve
items.summary: During the first day of Space Tech Expo Europe, SpaceNews’ Mike Gruss sits down with Pieter van Duijn, the chief technology officer of Loft Orbital. They discuss the growing level of trust in artificial intelligence in the commercial space industry, how using a satellite can be like renting a car and the obstacles to adoption. Satellites built in Denmark for the ultimate combination of pioneer and partner – where bold innovation meets absolute reliability. From modules to mini constellations of payload centric fleets, Space Inventor uniquely adapts to achieve your mission and to always – Make Space for Progress.

items.title: Putting a spotlight on AI, society, and humanity
items.summary: MIT students are going to office hours less often. They’re spending less time working through problem sets, and with one another. Those were among the findings of MIT’s recent report on artificial intelligence and education, and they are one reason a growing number of MIT faculty are concerned about how generative AI is both changing how people work and affecting how they think, learn, and relate to one another. For the MIT Human Insight Collaborative (MITHIC), those questions have become a central focus, and MITHIC is working with collaborators across the Institute, including the Social and Ethical Responsibilities of Computing (SERC), to help MIT address them.

items.title: Researchers find eight ways AI could lead to our downfall
items.summary: Government and academic assessments, including reports from the U.K. Government Office for Science and the RAND Corporation, have not ruled out the possibility that AI could lead to human extinction or societal collapse. To protect against such severe risks, we must first understand how those risks could unfold.

items.title: China Signals Its Intention to Land on Jupiter's Moon Callisto
items.summary: China is outlining plans to place a small lander on the surface of Jupiter's moon Callisto, the outermost of the four Galilean moons. It's an ambitious plan, and would be only the second time anything's landed on a Solar System body beyond Mars. But the payoff would be huge, even if the lander only carries its two proposed instruments.

items.title: Teens' TikTok stunt leads to bans from multiple West Valley schools
items.summary: A TikTok stunt by teenagers sneaking into West Valley high schools has led to their ban from multiple districts.

items.title: Robots learn human movement patterns to find paths through dense crowds
items.summary: Navigating a bustling train station or airport is a major challenge for people with visual impairments. New research from Örebro University teaches robots to follow the "unwritten rules" of human movement and make their way through dense crowds. In the long term, the technology could serve as a digital complement to guide dogs.

items.title: Anthropic set to price IPO in key test for AI boom
items.summary: Anthropic prices its blockbuster IPO on Wednesday, giving ordinary investors their first chance to bet directly on a stand-alone AI giant in a test of how long the artificial intelligence spending boom can last.

items.title: Chinese robots learn from humans in tech hub Shenzhen
items.summary: At a park refreshment stand in China's tech capital, Shenzhen, a humanoid robot grabs a cup and pulls a lever to form an ice cream spiral, then hands the customer their order.

items.title: AI-Powered Sashiko Introduces Experimental Patch Series Design Assessment
items.summary: When it comes to leveraging AI for Linux kernel development, one of the most widely-used solutions at the moment is Sashiko that has evolved nicely over the past year for agentic AI code review. This AI-driven screening of generated code posted to the Linux kernel mailing list constantly identifies bugs and other code defects in a quick and straight-forward manner. With being developed and maintained by Google engineers, it uses Gemini by default but is LLM-agnostic overall. Released on Tuesday was Sashiko v0.9.4 as the next step forward for this Linux kernel helper…

items.title: 4 More Anime Still Coming to Netflix in 2026
items.summary: 2026 is heading towards the final month of the year, as the Fall 2026 anime season will wrap up along with the year. The final quarter of the year began last month, when all major platforms released exciting new shows for fans worldwide. It’s no surprise that Crunchyroll had the biggest lineup, just like every other quarter. As the world’s largest anime streaming service, Crunchyroll releases dozens of series each quarter on a weekly schedule. On the other hand, Netflix has been venturing into the anime industry for the past few years with original series and new licenses.

items.title: AV Linux 25.3 for Content Creators Returns to Xfce by Default
items.summary: AV Linux 25.3, a Debian-based Linux distro for multimedia content creators, has been released, marking the return of Xfce as a fully integrated desktop environment alongside Enlightenment. AV Linux now boots into Xfce by default, but users can switch to Enlightenment from the LightDM login screen. According to developer Glen MacArthur, the decision to bring back Xfce was driven by user feedback. Some users were reluctant to adopt Enlightenment after the distribution’s earlier desktop transition, and the new release offers both environments without abandoning the existing Enlightenment integration.

items.title: FAA investigates how a router upgrade in Arkansas led to US ground stop
items.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is investigating how a routine router replacement at a radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, disrupted communications at 17 of its 22 en route air traffic control centers on November 13, 2026, forcing the agency to halt departures across the US for more than four hours. A central question the investigation is now focused on is why a different router in Amarillo, Texas, also began wreaking havoc on the system, despite the sites being more than 500 miles apart.

items.title: Winston Churchill Desperately Wanted a Wartime Meeting With FDR. He Got It, and Their Three-Week Christmas Summit Changed the Trajectory of WWII
items.summary: On the morning of December 10, 1941, Winston Churchill finished his massive breakfast in bed at No. 10 Downing Street, as was his custom, and opened his red box of official business. The telephone at his bedside rang. Admiral Dudley Pound, the first sea lord, was calling, but Churchill could not quite hear what he was saying. “His voice sounded odd,” Churchill later wrote. Then the words came clearly: The Japanese had sunk both the battleship Prince of Wales and the battle cruiser Repulse in the South China Sea, where the ships had been tasked with securing Britain’s Far East interests.

items.title: HBO Max’s ‘Lanterns’ Officially Confirms New 2027 Release
items.summary: As part of a decision to revamp the DCEU, James Gunn took charge as co-chairman and co-CEO of DC Studios on November 1, 2022, alongside co-CEO Peter Safran. During their time in corporate studio management for DC Studios, the pair had a Gods and Monsters vision with movies like Superman and Supergirl being made along with Creature Commandos. The plan was mainly a success, with the sci-fi spectacle of Superman leading the way and, despite Supergirl 's underwhelming reception, critically acclaimed projects like Lanterns and Clayface were a testament to the quality of their plan.

items.title: Galaxy Outflows Likely Regulate Star Formation At ‘Cosmic Noon’ NASA’s Webb Reveals
items.summary: Sitting here on the outskirts of our Milky Way Galaxy, itâs hard to imagine the galactic machinations that led to our goldilocks spot around a very welcoming yellow dwarf star. But for decades, astronomers have suspected that the internal dynamics of massive galaxies like ours play an outsized role in regulating star formation. As observations by NASAâs James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) now reveal, massive galaxies have largescale gaseous outflows that greatly quench their star production.

items.title: The Country's Oldest Operating Lighthouse Predates the American Revolution and Still Shines on New York Harbor After More Than 260 Years
items.summary: Until the 20th century, the only safe maritime route into New York Harbor zagged between shallow shoals. At one particularly treacherous point, the shipping lane bent around the northern tip of the Sandy Hook peninsula, which the English politician Thomas Pownall described in 1755 as “a neck of low sandy hills covered with cedars and holly, ending in a low sandy point.” After a devastating series of shipwrecks in 1761, New York’s merchants petitioned the Colonial Assembly to build a navigational aid.

items.title: Arizona aims for the stars with U.S. Space Academy proposal
items.summary: PHOENIX (AZFamily) — Arizona has a long history of space exploration, and now the state hopes to train NASA’s future astronauts. Arizona submitted its application to be home to the U.S. Space Academy, which would train future astronauts, engineers and technicians. The proposal outlines an interim campus at the Arizona State University’s Tempe campus in the Novus Innovation Corridor, a community at Rural Road and University Drive. It would immediately be ready for the first class of 300 students.

items.title: Here's how much rain fell across Phoenix area on Tuesday
items.summary: Some of the most rainfall was seen in the communities located north of Scottsdale.

items.title: Cosmo Bee to flight-test Honeybee Hall thruster with D-Orbit in 2027
items.summary: Daejeon, Republic of Korea – October 14, 2026: South Korean space electric propulsion startup Cosmo Bee plans to conduct an in-orbit flight test of its 10 mN-class Honeybee Hall thruster system in October 2027 through a service agreement with D-Orbit. Honeybee is a 10 mN-class Hall thruster system under development by Cosmo Bee for small satellites operating in LEO constellations. “In-orbit validation is an essential step as we prepare to bring Honeybee to the commercial market,” said Dongha Park, co-founder and CEO of Cosmo Bee.

items.title: Google bets on superhot geothermal to power Oregon data centers
items.summary: The geothermal startup Quaise Energy has landed a major first customer for its novel, superhot project in central Oregon. On Tuesday, the Houston-based firm announced that Google has agreed to buy 50 megawatts of carbon-free power from Quaise’s first commercial project, called Project Obsidian, near the Newberry…

items.title: Q&A: Why building math muscles remains important in the AI era
items.summary: John Urschel PhD ’21, the Class of 1956 Career Development Assistant Professor in the MIT Department of Mathematics, is no stranger to building muscle: Before earning his PhD at MIT, Urschel strengthened his offensive muscles as a lineman for the Baltimore Ravens. He remains committed to helping his students exercise, but now his focus is on critical thinking skills. In the classroom, Urschel shares with his students his lifelong love for solving puzzles, while honing their abilities to be strong qualitive thinkers — skills he argues will be essential in an artificial intelligence-enabled world.

items.title: Buckeye officer injured while trying to stop suspected drunk driver, police say
items.summary: A driver allegedly rammed two police cars, injuring an officer, Buckeye police said.

items.title: Meet Linde Freya Tangelder, Nendo's pick for the most influential designer of the next 20 years
items.summary: Nendo has selected Linde Freya Tangelder for Dezeen's 20×20 project in partnership with Kohler. In this interview, the Dutch designer explains why she doesn't find design inspiring. Insofar as she creates furniture and lighting, Tangelder is technically a designer, but only just. "How I think is not typical design," she told Dezeen. "So I'm never thinking about function in the first place. The whole process is very intuitive, it's just a cloud of connections in my head – more about concepts or stories that I want to tell rather than making a functional piece."

items.title: Codeberg Domain Suspended by NameSilo, Disrupting Open-Source Projects
items.summary: Codeberg, the non-profit Git hosting platform and a popular alternative to GitHub, has been taken offline after its domain registrar, NameSilo, unexpectedly suspended the codeberg.org domain. The service is currently inaccessible as a result. The outage started on 18th November with Codeberg confirming the issue in a Mastodon post. They stated the domain had simply vanished from their NameSilo account and they had no idea what had occurred. Codeberg very quickly ruled out a number of potential explanations.

items.title: Gaming lab opens at Glendale Community College
items.summary: Big news for students who are interested in gaming at Glendale Community College, as the school has opened a new gaming lab, giving students a dedicated space to compete, connect, and create. FOX 10's Irene Snyder has more.

items.title: 19th-Century Philosopher’s Head Examined
items.summary: LONDON, ENGLAND—English philosopher Jeremy Bentham suffered from painful toothaches and arthritis of the lower jaw, according to a statement released by University College London. Bentham is thought to have been the first person to have legally registered the preference for his body to be used for scientific study after death, including preservation as an “auto-icon,” or “self-image.” After his death in June 11, 1832, Bentham’s remains were dissected and his body preserved in the collections of University College London.

items.title: Bashas' water tower demolished in south Chandler to make way for new homes
items.summary: Tuesday marked the end of an era for one South Chandler community. After decades of standing tall over this neighborhood, the Bashas' water tower was officially demolished. Neighbors stood along Basha Road, watching as crews cut and tipped the water tower until it fell. "It was a surreal experience; it's a little bit sad," said Megan Craghead, who grew up in this neighborhood and is now raising her family here. Through the years, the water tower was always there.

items.title: Child in critical condition after being pulled from water in Mesa neighborhood
items.summary: A child is in critical condition after being pulled from the water at a Mesa home Tuesday afternoon. According to the Mesa Police Department, first responders were called to the area near Crimson Road and Madero Avenue around 3:21 p.m. after receiving reports of a possible child drowning. CPR was already being performed when Mesa Fire arrived, and the child was taken to the hospital in critical condition. At this time, the circumstances surrounding the incident are unclear. This is a developing story. ABC15 will continue to keep you updated as soon as we receive more information.

items.title: Silver prices find $50 floor as solar industry seeks to accelerate shift toward copper
items.summary: Silver prices appear to have stabilized around $50 per ounce following an exceptionally volatile year, but the photovoltaic industry should not expect a return to the much lower prices of previous decades, according to Philip Newman, managing director of Metals Focus. “I think the price, the floor seems quite strong, but I think you’re still going to see more volatility,” Newman told pv magazine. “Could prices dip below 50? Of course they can. But I think the 50 still seems like a decent floor.”

items.title: Can AI help build a healthier future?
items.summary: Technical advancement is moving at such a rapid pace that it can be challenging to define the tomorrow we’re working toward. In The Shape of Things to Come, Microsoft Research leader Doug Burger and experts from across disciplines tease out the thorniest AI issues facing technologists, policymakers, business decisionmakers, and other stakeholders today. The goal: to amplify the shared understanding needed to build a future in which the AI transition is a net positive.

items.title: BMZ integrates digital battery passports into series production
items.summary: BMZ, together with Minespider, is introducing digital battery passports for its EU production in Germany and Poland. The passports are to be created directly using production data and will meet the requirements of the EU Battery Regulation starting February 2027.

items.title: Duke Energy Florida aims to deliver $1 billion in customer savings with four new solar projects
items.summary: Duke Energy Florida filed regulatory applications for four new photovoltaic facilities in Orange and Sumter counties. The utility projects that the combined portfolio will deliver approximately $1 billion in customer savings over a 30-year operational life primarily by displacing fossil fuel generation. This expansion aligns with Florida’s broader clean energy momentum. According to the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA), Florida ranks 3rd in the United States for total installed solar capacity, boasting 22.5 GW of operational solar that powers over 2.7 million homes.

items.title: A 16th-Century Castle in England Is Falling Into the Ocean, Sparking a Debate Over Whether It Should Be Saved or Allowed to Disintegrate With Dignity
items.summary: For centuries, Hurst Castle, built on England’s south coast by Henry VIII in 1544 to protect the passage to Portsmouth, was unassailable. Through Tudor spats with France and the Holy Roman Empire, the English Civil War, skirmishes with Napoleon and both world wars, the squat artillery fort was garrisoned and at the ready, but never once attacked. After sitting almost at sea level for four centuries unchallenged, the castle is now under attack from a different sort of enemy, one even more pernicious than the French.

items.title: Trump shakes hands with Putin and Xi ahead of historic talks in China
items.summary: Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin met for the first time in over a year on Wednesday, as the pair prepared for landmark talks in China with Xi Jinping. The US president was greeted off his plane by the Chinese leader as he arrived in Shenzhen for a summit of Asia-Pacific leaders, which will culminate in a closely-watched meeting between the pair and the Russian president. After a carefully choreographed handshake and hug between Trump and Xi on the tarmac, the US president later greeted and exchanged pleasantries with Putin ahead of a reception.

items.title: EU accelerates approvals for power grids and charging stations
items.summary: The European Parliament and EU member states have reached a provisional agreement to streamline approval procedures for grid connections, charging stations, storage systems, and more. As part of this, the construction of charging stations with up to one megawatt in "artificial structures" is expected to become exempt from approval in the future.

items.title: Discord’s Linux app sure did improve a lot this year
items.summary: Discord recently shared a potted roundup of improvements made to its Linux app this year, including smarter updating, better screen sharing on Wayland and working push-to-talk. Their Discord <3 Linux: A Year of Upgrades blog post also reveals that per-app audio sharing is finally coming to Wayland-based desktops, though it’s not ready for testing just yet. As I don’t personally use Discord that often, the roundup was an interesting read for me. Notable, Discord’s Linux installer was made a lot smaller.

items.title: Phosh 0.59 Linux Mobile Shell Adds Voice Input, New Quick Settings
items.summary: Phosh, the GNOME-based mobile shell for Linux smartphones and other touch-enabled devices, has released version 0.59. One of the most interesting additions is initial speech input support in Stevia, Phosh’s on-screen keyboard. The feature uses Vosk, an offline speech recognition toolkit, enabling voice-based text entry. However, the implementation is still in its early stages. The quick settings panel gains two new controls. The first lets users capture screenshots directly without external tools, while the second provides a way to start or stop the SSH daemon.

items.title: BMW's First U.S.-Made EV Is Now Rolling Off The Assembly Line
items.summary: BMW’s plant in Spartanburg, South Carolina, is now building the company’s new iX5 electric SUV. It’s the first mass-produced EV built by BMW in the United States. The electric SUV will be joined by five more EVs by the end of the decade. The first American-made electric BMW is now being assembled at the company’s plant in Spartanburg, South Carolina. It’s a big moment for the German automaker in the U.S., but it’s just the beginning of a much larger plan, which will include no fewer than six U.S.-built EVs by the end of the decade.

items.title: TokenEconomizer: Learning from Experience to Make AI Coding Agents More Efficient
items.summary: At a glance Developers use AI coding agents in the same codebases day after day, yet agents often start each session from scratch: rediscovering familiar facts, loading unused tools, and repeating unsuccessful approaches. TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that learns from an agent’s past sessions in a repository to reduce waste in future sessions, without modifying the agent or its underlying model. Across 277 real bug-fixing tasks, TokenEconomizer reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agents.

items.title: Building the Agent Host Protocol for sessions that continue across devices
items.summary: Models are now good enough to work for hours or even days on their own. You don’t have to watch over every thing they do, but you still need to be able to check in, no matter where you are. An agent can’t live only inside one application. The work should continue even If you close a window or switch devices. In GitHub Copilot you can start an agent session in one place and pick it up in another. This session continuity runs on the Agent Host Protocol (AHP), an open standard built first in VS Code and adopted across GitHub.

items.title: Solarcycle, PedalPoint Recycling merge to feed a $7.4B US metals refinery
items.summary: Old solar panels have silver and copper worth recovering. A new US recycling company called Jupiter plans to send metals recovered from retired solar panels and data center hardware to Korea Zinc’s refineries, including a $7.4 billion plant planned for Clarksville, Tennessee. more…

items.title: EV Owners Aren’t Worried About Their Batteries. They’re Worried About Myths
items.summary: 74% of surveyed EV owners identified myths as a leading barrier to adoption, ahead of price and apartment charging. Battery longevity topped the list of misconceptions, yet 65% weren’t worried about their own battery’s lifespan. The survey reflects existing owners’ views, rather than directly measuring why other buyers avoid EVs. The battery always seems to be the big thing people cite as a key concern with electric cars. Will it need replacing? Will it catch fire? And what happens to your local electricity grid when everybody plugs in their EVs at the same time?

items.title: Who to watch in Spain's election race
items.summary: Spanish voters face a snap election on 29 November, with the conservatives leading most polls after eight years of Socialist-led rule under Pedro SÃ¡nchez. When combined with the far-right Vox, they could secure a majority. The left had hoped to focus on Spain's housing crisis, but the government has been buffeted by corruption scandals, a migrant crisis, and most recently two rail disasters that left 115 people dead. Here are the key figures to look out for in the race to run Spain's next government.

items.title: Fire Retardant Linked to Serious Airtanker Corrosion
items.summary: The National Transportation Safety Board is calling on the U.S. Forest Service to strengthen its corrosion testing requirements for aerial firefighting retardants after an investigation identified extensive damage to two large airtankers. In a report released this month, the NTSB determined that the agency’s existing qualification process failed to adequately evaluate the effects of a magnesium chloride-based retardant on aircraft structures. Corrosion Found on Airtankers The investigation involved a British Aerospace BAe-146 operated by Neptune Aviation Services and an MD-87 operated by Aero Air.

items.title: Iceland’s first wind farm comes with a water-saving bonus
items.summary: Iceland’s first utility-scale wind farm comes with a useful perk: When the wind picks up, its hydropower reservoirs can save water for later. Vaðölduver Wind Farm plugs straight into the existing Búrfell hydropower infrastructure, sharing 220 kV transmission lines, substations, and access roads. And Iceland’s windiest months coincide with the time of year when less water flows into its reservoirs. Once complete, Vaðölduver will have 120 megawatts (MW) of capacity. When I met with the folks at Landsvirkjun in Reykjavik last month, they told me that’s enough to power the equivalent of 90,000 Icelandic households.

items.title: In the South, heat pumps are the secret to a more reliable grid
items.summary: For many in North Carolina and Tennessee, 2022’s Winter Storm Elliott lives in infamy. Temperatures plunged well below freezing for days at a time, just as families were gathered at home for the Christmas holiday. The grid couldn’t keep up, and some 1.6 million households lost power in rolling blackouts in those two…

items.title: Nurse spends $50,000 on a new car to drive home after US flights grounded
items.summary: A woman splashed out on a $50,000 car so that she could get home during the nationwide air travel stop in the United States, and ended up driving for 27 hours. Back on November 13, travel plans across the United States were plunged into chaos after a nationwide ground stop was put on planes. The stoppage saw 20,000 flights disrupted, leaving passengers to miss getting home, traveling for work, and delayed for at least a day. In true Planes, Trains, and Automobiles fashion, some travellers set out to find alternative modes of transport as a result of the group stoppage.

items.title: Earth Faces Extinction In Netflix’s ‘3 Body Problem’ Season 2 Teaser
items.summary: They haven’t flown 24 trillion miles to negotiate. The alien invasion gets nearer in season two of Netflix’s blockbuster series 3 Body Problem; the first teaser sees Earth potentially on the cusp of extinction. The Emmy-nominated series returns globally on January 14, 2027, only on Netflix. In season two, “As the alien invasion nears, humanity prepares to meet them — on Earth and beyond. While a space fleet embarks on a mission that spans centuries, a secret locked inside of one man’s mind might be humanity’s only hope for survival.”

items.title: New net-zero community will become Michigan’s first virtual power plant
items.summary: Mitch Hall and his wife, Lori, live in one of the most sustainable communities in the U.S. Their town house is among a few dozen residences constructed so far at Veridian at County Farm, a fossil-fuel-free, net-zero-energy development in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Homes here make about as much solar energy as they…

items.title: Import AI 481: AI sub-contractors; a wet lab for AI; and subterfuge during development
items.summary: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe. Subscribe now AI systems are getting good at sub-contracting to make themselves better: …AI can now productively spend money to improve itself… Researchers have developed FrontierML, a benchmark “that measures how well agents turn capital into model performance on challenging, end-to-end machine learning tasks.” It shows that today’s frontier systems are already able to, when given some money, turn this into improving their own performance on a basket of 21 distinct tasks.

items.title: “We're not saying they're perfect” says architect fighting to save Melbourne's public housing blocks
items.summary: Architect Simon Robinson has been leading calls for the Victorian state government to rethink its plan to demolish all of Melbourne ’s public housing towers. In this interview, he sets out why he believes retrofit is the smarter approach. Announced by the Labor-run state government in 2023, Homes Victoria ’s High-Rise Redevelopment Program (HRRP) will see all 44 of Melbourne's public housing towers and many other lower-rise blocks razed and replaced with new housing by 2051. Officials argue that the buildings, constructed between 1962 and 1975, have reached the end of their useful lives.

items.title: The Best Thanksgiving Side Recipes, According to Eater Editors
items.summary: The sides are objectively the best part of Thanksgiving, and it’s not even an argument. Mashed potatoes and stuffing are the reason we’re all convening at the table, right? Aaaaand the whole “gathering with loved ones” thing too, of course. While we’ve all got our staples, the sides are also the opportunity to really have fun with the meal and showcase whatever new ideas have been simmering since last year’s big meal. They’re our chance to create a menu with balance, adding a bright, crunchy salad that perfectly offsets the richness of all those buttery potatoes or offering an essential hit of cozy baked pasta with melty cheese.

items.title: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI partner to bring Le Figaro journalism to ChatGPT
items.summary: Le Groupe Figaro and OpenAI partner to bring Le Figaro’s journalism to ChatGPT through summaries and excerpts, with links to original stories.

items.title: Fed’s Waller says central bank may need to ‘shock people’ with half-point rate hike
items.summary: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller on Wednesday called for aggressive action against inflation, saying the central bank need to "shock people" as prices continue to rise more than he expected. In the near term, the policymaker told CNBC in a live interview that a half-percentage-point increase in the Fed's benchmark rate is probably necessary at the Dec. 8-9 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee. He said the Fed needs to reverse the three quarter-point reductions from last year and may need to do more.

items.title: Lowe's posts strong online sales, raises outlook despite slow housing market
items.summary: Lowe's on Wednesday posted strong quarterly results and raised its full-year outlook as the company said it saw strength among professional shoppers. The company said comparable sales grew 1.8% for the quarter, driven by a 17.4% increase in online sales and "solid" performance in pro and home services sales. Net sales grew to $22.76 billion. Because of the strength, Lowe's now said it expects full-year sales of roughly $92.5 billion, up from a previous projection of $92 billion. It also expects comparable sales to be up 0.5%, compared to previous guidance of flat.

items.title: China and the U.S. are still the biggest polluters, but only China is doing better
items.summary: As more than 200 countries meet in Turkey for the annual United Nations climate talks, COP31, the two largest emitters of greenhouse gases remain China and the United States. Now the countries' stories are diverging. For years, China's climate pollution was growing, driven by increased coal use. But for the past two and a half years, China's emissions have been flat or falling. items.title: The Four Draughtsmen
items.summary: By Henry Dudeney: Here is a queer new puzzle that I know will interest my readers considerably. The four draughtsmen are shown exactly as they stood on a square chequered board — not necessarily eight squares by eight — but the ink with which the board was drawn was evanescent, so that all the diagram except the men has disappeared. How many squares were there in the board and how am I to reconstruct it? I know that each man stood in the middle of a square, one on the edge of each side of the board and no man in a corner. It is a real puzzle, until you hit on the method of solution, and then to get the correct answer is absurdly easy.

items.title: Young Americans have no memory of AIDS at its worst – they’re still at risk of infection, even when HIV doesn’t feel like a threat

items.title: Eagles are eating human-sized baboons in the Sahara desert

In this region in the middle of the Sahara Desert about the size of Switzerland, the olive baboons ( Papio anubis ) have lived a separate life away from other primate species. At 40 to 60 pounds, some olive baboons are about the size of our early hominin ancestors. But their size does not keep them safe from hungry Verreaux’s eagles ( Aquila verreauxii ). New research published today in the American Journal of Biological Anthropology details how these eagles appear to be preying upon these nearly human-sized baboons.

Speaking during a Nov. 15 interview with French broadcaster RTL, Trappier said the technology presents significant challenges for larger aircraft, particularly the company’s Falcon business jets. Technical Challenges Trappier pointed to hydrogen storage requirements and limitations involving aircraft weight, available space and range. He specifically questioned whether the technology could support an aircraft comparable in size to Dassault’s Falcon 10X, which completed its first flight in June.

items.title: Turkish Akinci and TB2 UCAVs Conduct Highway Operations
items.summary: Baykar said this is the first in a series of trials to develop runway-independent capabilities, which will be followed by similar tests involving its other homegrown drones. Baykar’s Akinci and TB2 Unmanned Combat Aerial Vehicles (UCAV) reached a major milestone when they conducted their first highway operations on Nov. 12, 2026, the Turkish defense company announced on Nov. 13. Overseen by the Ministry of National Defense and the Directorate General of Highways, the operation “demonstrated the ability of indigenous platforms to perform missions without relying on runways,” said a statement.

items.title: Serbian MiG-29 fighter crashes near Belgrade, killing pilot
items.summary: A Serbian Air Force and Air Defense MiG-29 fighter crashed near Stara Pazova, northwest of Belgrade, on November 17, 2026, killing its pilot, Major Goran Bulajić, according to Serbia’s Ministry of Defense. The aircraft, assigned to the 204th Air Brigade, went down at around 08:45 local time, the ministry said in a statement carried by Serbian broadcaster N1. Bulajić had served in the Serbian Armed Forces since 1996. The aircraft crashed in a field between Nova Pazova and Stara Pazova, according to Serbian media reports.

items.title: Former Dishonored designer joins the team on New Blood's Victorian immersive sim Gloomwood, with a new level and new weapons coming this year
items.summary: Gloomwood, the Victorian survival horror immersive sim (or, wait, I'm getting reports that we shouldn't call it an immersive sim, apparently ) by Dillon Rogers is a game that is quite happily inspired by its predecessors such as Thief, Resident Evil and Dishonored; you could call it 'Thief with guns', if you really wanted to. (Sorry, I've just seen that the domain for Gloomwood's site used to be 'residenthievil.com'. Wonderful). Now, that last inspiration has come full circle, as publisher New Blood Interactive's latest update post confirms that the newest member of the team is none other than former Dishonored designer Julien Eveillé.

items.title: Hyperscale data centers use 2% of US electricity
items.summary: One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built. A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025.

items.title: China’s Largest Uncrewed Cargo Aircraft Completes First Flight
items.summary: Chinese aircraft developer Air White Whale said it has completed the first flight of its W5000 uncrewed cargo aircraft, which the company describes as the world’s largest aircraft of its kind. According to a Nov. 16 announcement from China’s Changzhou municipal government, the aircraft completed a 30-minute test flight Saturday at Otog Front Banner General Aviation Airport in Inner Mongolia. Flight Testing During the flight, the W5000 reached approximately 3,300 feet above the airport and maintained an indicated airspeed of about 119 knots.

items.title: Dungeons & Dragons Officially Announces Its Next Forgotten Realms Release For March 2027
items.summary: The Forgotten Realms is one of the most legendary campaign settings in Dungeons & Dragons, if not the most. This is evident from the fact that some of the franchise's most iconic media takes place in this world, including 2023's Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves, Baldur's Gate 3 (2023), and R.A. Salvatore's hugely popular fantasy series, The Legend of Drizzt. Now, fans have another Forgotten Realms release to look forward to this coming spring.

items.title: Ted Raimi talks Your Dearest, Darkest Friend, his new horror talk show on Screambox
items.summary: Ted Raimi has spent decades entertaining fans with memorable performances in movies and television, but now the genre veteran is inviting viewers into his own strange little corner of the horror world. Raimi is the host of Your Dearest, Darkest Friend with Ted Raimi, an unconventional interview series on the Screambox streaming service. JoBlo’s Tyler Nichols recently sat down with Raimi to discuss the show, and you can check out the interview in the embed above. The series premiered on Screambox on October 30, 2026, bringing horror industry personalities into Raimi’s wonderfully creepy world for conversations, cocktails, and some spooky entertainment.

items.title: Planning a Ski Trip This Winter? There’s a Way to Save Up to 65% on Lift Tickets
items.summary: Ski vacations have a way of getting expensive before you’ve even set foot on the mountain. Between lodging, equipment rentals, lift tickets, and the occasional après-ski cocktail, a long weekend in the snow can add up quickly. But we’ve got a hot tip every traveler should know: You could save up to 65% on lift tickets simply by purchasing the right ski pass ahead of time. And no, you don’t have to be someone who spends every weekend on the slopes to take advantage of it. With ski season already underway at Colorado favorites like Vail, Breckenridge, and Keystone, there’s still time to get in on the savings.

items.title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place
items.summary: On Monday, the Supreme Court announced it would not hear an appeal of a lower court decision that blocked the government from canceling the grants of a handful of researchers whose funding had been revoked during the Trump administration's purge of DEI-related work. While the decision applies to only seven researchers in California, the lower court had ruled that the government's actions violated the First Amendment and so may have broad implications. The Supreme Court provided no discussion of its rejection, and no justices filed a dissent regarding the decision.

items.title: Disney Plus and Hulu will be a fully unified experience in December
items.summary: us will become a fully unified experience in December. TikTok content will also be introduced to the platform next month. Disney did not say when the Hulu app will shut down. Hulu has long been on a crash course to merge with Disney Plus. Despite that, the two platforms are still standalone apps. While the integration initially started back in 2023, Disney is nearly ready to finally complete the unification. In a fourth-quarter earnings report, Walt Disney Company CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston revealed when they plan to fully unify the two streaming apps. The target window is December; however, the CEO and CFO did not offer an exact date.

items.title: United Airlines System Outage Delays Flights Nationwide
items.summary: United Airlines temporarily delayed departing flights across the country Monday following a systemwide technology outage that affected several applications used by its pilots. The disruption lasted approximately 90 minutes before the airline restored service. According to an internal memo from the Air Line Pilots Association obtained by ABC News, the outage affected crew communications and messaging systems. The airline was also unable to provide final aircraft weights required for departure calculations.

items.title: MNT Reform Next, the ultra-open laptop, starts shipping
items.summary: Before Framework took the idea of modular, easily upgradable laptops mainstream, there was the MNT Reform, a laptop with openness in every part of its design. I was pleased to see see (via notebookcheck) it’s started shipping high-end Hyper configurations of its laptop model, the MNT Reform Next, to backers of its 2025 crowdfunding campaign via Crowd Supply. These are going out later than originally planned – autumn 2025, initially – due to the various setbacks and hurdles that come with designing, engineering and manufacturing a truly open laptop, including firmware.

items.title: Singapore Airlines A350 Suffers Another Mid-Air Smoke Scare Within a Week
items.summary: SINGAPORE- A Rockhampton Airport (ROK) diversion involving a Singa pore Airlines (SQ) Airbus A350-900 has raised further questions after the same aircraft returned to the Australian airport for a second time in less than a week. The aircraft, registered as 9V-SHA, turned back shortly after departure on November 17, 2026, when smoke was detected inside its cabin. Unlike its previous incident, the aircraft was not carrying fare-paying passengers. Seven Singapore Airlines employees, including two pilots, were on board during the ferry flight from Rockhampton, Queensland, towards Singapore.

items.title: The Restaurant With The Absolute Best Ribeye In Your State, Hands Down
items.summary: Not much makes a meal feel more indulgent than an impeccably prepared steak. And all the better if that steak is a wondrous ribeye. We're talking gorgeous marbling, rich beefy flavor, and those delectable rivulets of fat that practically melt like butter, right into the meat as it sizzles. items.title: When Jorge Luis Borges Co-Wrote a Surreal Sci-Fi Noir Film: Invasión (1969)
items.summary: “ La ciudad es más que la gente. ” So declares a character called Don Porfirio in Invasión, the debut feature by Argentine director Hugo Santiago. The line is the film’s most memorable, not least because of the reversal it pulls on our expectations. Saying that a city is really its people must have been a somewhat banal observation even in 1969, when Invasión came out, but saying that a city is more than its people still sounds contrarian enough to be intriguing.

items.title: Kotlin Toolchain 0.14: Agentic Development and iOS Publishing
items.summary: The Kotlin Toolchain helps you build and ship multiplatform apps faster, with less setup and configuration. Its CLI provides a unified workflow for building, running, testing, and publishing apps for Android, iOS, desktop, and web, whether you’re developing with AI agents or writing code yourself. items.title: US indicts Irish man over destruction of C-130H at Shannon Airport
items.summary: US federal prosecutors have indicted an Irish man over an attack on a US Air National Guard C-130H Hercules at Shannon Airport (SNN) on April 11, 2026, saying the military transport aircraft was so extensively damaged that it will never fly again. The aircraft, valued at approximately $60 million, was rendered inoperable and effectively destroyed, according to the US Department of Justice (DOJ). Its tail section has since been removed by US authorities as part of efforts to store and dismantle the aircraft.

items.title: Whale snot helps scientists sequence an entire genome
items.summary: Whale vomit can be turned into expensive perfume. Whale carcasses will sink to the bottom and become marine life habitats. Whale pee nourishes the entire ocean. But how about whale snot? The microbes and other biological material emitted from their blowholes when the giant cetaceans breathe has helped scientists sequence an entire whale genome: Take that whale vomit. The findings are detailed in a study published today in the journal Molecular Ecology Resources. Drones and snot Whole genomes are crucial for animal conservation.

items.title: 28 Seats: European Carrier Reveals First-Ever Premium Economy Cabin For US Routes
items.summary: Irish flag carrier Aer Lingus has become the latest airline to join the premium economy revolution, with the airline having just unveiled its new product offering ahead of its launch next October. It plans to fit 28 spacious recliner seats on ten of its Airbus A330 widebody twinjets. This will represent the bulk of its twin-aisle fleet, with ch-aviation showing that it currently has two Airbus A330-200s and 12 A330-300s.

items.title: Robert Eggers Says ‘Werwulf’ Is So Scary, He Felt “Physically Ill” Writing It
items.summary: As a lifelong fan of werewolf movies, I’m practically foaming at the mouth for Robert Eggers ‘ Werwulf at this point. And the filmmaker is out here adding fuel to that fire. In a recent chat with Empire, Eggers revealed that, with Werwulf, he set out to make the scariest film of his career. Said the director, “ You’re always trying to stretch yourself, and I thought, ‘Let me try to write the scariest horror movie I can write.’ It’s definitely the darkest. ” If the guy who made The Witch and Nosferatu is saying that Werwulf is his “darkest” film, we had better believe we are in for one sinister werewolf movie, because those pics are bleak.

items.title: Your gut bacteria helps your body keep track of time, and when you eat influences how much nutrition you get from food
items.summary: How your body processes food is significantly influenced by daily rhythms tied to 24-hour light-dark cycles. In new research published in the scientific journal Cell Host & Microbe, my colleagues and I found that the microbes living in your gut are the hidden timekeepers behind this system. Gut microbes convert dietary signals into molecules that intestinal cells use to synchronize nutrient absorption with feeding times. In mice, this microbe-controlled timing mechanism maximizes the nutrients the mouse’s body takes in and supports growth, especially when food is scarce.

items.title: We Tracked The World’s Busiest Aircraft For A Week: Island Hoppers Vs Long-Haul Workhorses
items.summary: Using the new Simple Flying Flight Tracker, we examined the world's busiest aircraft. A Divi Divi Air Twin Otter and a Hawaiian Airlines Boeing 717 each completed 75 flights in one week, making them the world's busiest individual aircraft by flight count. However, when looking at the time spent airborne, the results are completely different. An Air New Zealand Boeing 787-9 and an SAS Airbus A350-900 each recorded approximately 134 hours in the air during the same period, equivalent to roughly 19 hours per day.

items.title: Inspiring FOSS project Crosspoint Reader has lessons about tech, communities, and LLMs
items.summary: The Ubuntu Summit isn't all about Ubuntu, or even Linux. The second day opened with a talk from CrossPoint Reader project lead Justin Mitchell, with both good and bad news for all kinds of FOSS. items.title: AIR Sends Cargo Drone to Florida
items.summary: Israeli aircraft manufacturer AIR VEV said Monday that it has shipped its first AIR 120D autonomous cargo aircraft to the United States for planned flight demonstrations in Auburndale, Florida. items.title: How to Decide Which Ski Pass Is Best For Your Winter Travel Plans
items.summary: With snow already falling in the Rockies and a strong El Niño weather pattern expected to benefit certain US mountain regions, skiers and riders are already dusting off their gear and booking their winter trips. Of course, skiing and snowboarding aren’t typically budget-friendly sports. Once you factor in meals, lodging, and transportation in addition to a lift ticket (which costs well over $300 per day at several US resorts), it’s almost worth taking out a loan to pay for a one-week family ski trip.

items.title: Well-Traveled Women on Where They Plan to Visit in 2027
items.summary: A bucket list item is one thing—turning it into an itinerary is another. The difference often lies in deciding that the places we dream about are worth pursuing amid limited vacation days and financial constraints. It’s a sentiment captured by avid traveler and content creator, Lucrenzia Worthington: “If there's one thing I've learned, it's that it’s never the right time, only the time you finally decide to go.” With 2027 in sight, we’re taking inspiration from well-traveled women who are already thinking about the possibilities of the fresh, new year ahead and the trips they hope to pull off.

items.title: 4 Lesser-Known Sci-Fi Movies That Scored Over 90% With Audiences on Rotten Tomatoes
items.summary: Unfortunately, not every good movie becomes popular, and there are many reasons why that happens. But when it comes to sci-fi, that’s a bit of a shame, given how much the genre has to offer and how interesting it could be to see these stories reach a wider audience. Maybe you’ve come across some movies that flew under the radar, discovered titles almost nobody talks about, or found others that somehow seem to have disappeared from everyone’s memories. items.title: NVIDIA and Lambda Disclose First Production Co-Packaged Optics Cluster… It is FINALLY real
items.summary: For SC26, NVIDIA and Lambda discussed their first production co-packaged optics (CPO) cluster. The industry has worked to move CPO from the lab to production for decades. Many in the industry will tell you it is a few years out, but Lambda has already deployed it in production in a cluster with over 10,000 GPUs. We covered NVIDIA’s co-packaged optics extensively during the company’s Hot Chips 2025 presentation. NVIDIA’s first version of the packaging is in its Quantum-X switching product, while Spectrum-X will be an updated second-generation part.

items.title: Datadog Brings Production Experimentation to AI Agent Observability
items.summary: Datadog is extending its Agent Observability platform with Online Experiments, allowing engineering teams to compare AI agent versions against real production traffic rather than relying exclusively on predefined evaluation datasets. The capability combines agent evaluation scores with operational measurements such as latency, token consumption, execution cost, and errors, helping teams establish whether changes to models, prompts, retrieval strategies, or tools actually improve an agent. The announcement addresses a growing challenge in agent development: a change that performs better in a controlled test may behave very differently when exposed to unpredictable user requests.

items.title: The Greek Myth That Inspired the Hunger Games
items.summary: Within the crumbling ruins of the ancient palace of Knossos on the Greek island of Crete, a labyrinth is said to have once existed. No evidence of the labyrinth has been found, but the Greek myth that tells its story has immortalized it forever in the realm of the imagination. Like many foundational stories, this one has been told and retold in many forms, weaving itself into the cultural landscape and inspiring everyone from Sigmund Freud and Plato to Suzanne Collins, author of the Hunger Games series.

items.title: A Man and His Muse AI Agent Sue Meta
items.summary: In his 6,500-word manifesto earlier this year, Mark Zuckerberg said people would use Meta’s AI agents to “work 24/7 on your behalf to improve your relationships, health, career, finances, home management, hobbies, and more.” Just a few months after that pronouncement, a man in South Carolina named Joe Thomas has used Meta’s Muse agent to sue Meta after the company’s content moderation filters locked his epoxy countertop business’s Facebook page after he gave his agent, “Baby Mia,” access to the account.

items.title: Why This It-Girl Ski Brand Is My Go-To Every Single Winter
items.summary: If there’s one thing I take almost as seriously as chasing some good snow, it’s having the right wardrobe to go with it. I’m a lifelong snowboarder, a fairly recent convert to skiing, and someone who has spent plenty of winters bouncing between mountains on the east coast and out west. I’ve learned that the best of the best ski gear needs to do a lot more than look good in a lodge photo. It has to hold up through long lift rides, changing conditions, unexpected snowfall, and the occasional unglamorous tumble.

items.title: Every State's Favorite Thanksgiving Pie, Mapped
items.summary: If you leave room for dessert on Thanksgiving night, there are plenty of options to choose from, especially when it comes to pie. Thanksgiving is known for pumpkin pie, but that's not the only choice depending on where you live. So which type of pie does your state prefer? items.title: Spirit Crossing, the new Zelda-ish hangout MMO from the creators of Cozy Grove, understands that sometimes you just want to be alone
items.summary: New multiplayer game Spirit Crossing offers up a visually blissful, but inwardly draconian world in which other people are not allowed to talk to you – indeed, not permitted access to the visible electromagnetic spectrum – unless you have given them a high five. By default, players appear to each other as shadows, all exploring a skybound landscape of magic animals and layer-cake mountains that reminds me of both Sable and The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom. items.title: You can now see and edit what Google Gemini remembers about you
items.summary: Editing the AI’s memory is one way you can shape its responses. Besides the ability to connect and use other applications and services, a lot of AI assistants' utility comes from their capacity to shape their responses based on what they learn and remember about you. Google's Personal Intelligence feature allows Gemini to pull in context from Gmail, YouTube, Search and other Google apps, and the AI also builds out its memory based on your preferences and other personal facts that come up in chats.

items.title: 'Defense by ChatGPT'
items.summary: We've written a lot about how AI generated writing has collided with – and created chaos for – the legal system in the last few years, from lawyers using it to do their research and filings for them to judges getting extremely fed up with dealing with these attorneys. In some cases, judges have sanctioned offending attorneys thousands of dollars for using AI to do their jobs, and lawyers give endless excuses when they're busted, with some calling it a “cautionary tale." items.title: Oregon is the latest state to sue OpenAI over child safety
items.summary: The state’s lawsuit calls on the company to address child safety issues and pay at least $2 billion in damages. Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield has filed a lawsuit accusing OpenAI of endangering the state's children, misleading the public about the safety of its product and violating the state's Unlawful Trade Practices Act. items.title: Best Places to Visit in December (United States)
